additional_considerations.rationale: Plausible, but hard to reconcile with CVA tenderness unless there is metastasis to a right posterior rib.
Classic triad is hematuria, flank pain and a palpable mass, often with constitutional symptoms; the other urinary symptoms could be from coexisting BPH.
No hypertension or volume overload argues against it, but IgA nephropathy often presents with an episode of gross hematuria, usually with a URI, GI symptoms or a flu-like illness.
Can cause hematuria but is uncommon in men, and there are no symptoms of acute infection.

source_issues: p024: the answer field also contains an examinee tip that belongs to the script, not the patient ("Prior to the social history, you may say, 'Some of the following questions may seem a bit uncomfortable...'"). Only the alcohol answer was annotated.

p013: topic is 'Onset of the previous symptoms' but the question asks whether he has experienced anything like this before; the onset of the urinary symptoms (frequency, straining, nocturia, weak stream, dribbling) is never given. The referent of 'it' in 'They mentioned that it's a part of aging' is unclear; the challenging question applies it to the blood in the urine.
p013 and p018 ask almost the same question (previous similar episodes); both are answered 'No'.
Alcohol amount: script says 'a few beers after work, about two to three times a week'; the note says '2 beers 2-3 times per week'.
Note PSH is written in the first person ('I had an appendectomy when I was 23'), copied from the script.
Note HPI says 'no changes in appetite'; the script asked about weight and dietary habits, not appetite.

Gold diagnosis #2 lists 'Right costovertebral angle tenderness', an exam finding, under History Finding(s); the Physical Finding(s) of all three diagnoses are N/A although the note exam records right CVA tenderness. Kept as given in the source.
Gold diagnosis #3 lists 'Polyuria'; the patient describes increased frequency (every 2-3 hours), not increased volume.

The patient denies abdominal and back pain (p006), while the SP is told to show pain on right CVA tenderness testing and the note exam records mild right CVA tenderness; not contradictory (spontaneous pain vs. elicited tenderness) but worth noting.
gold_additional_diagnosis: 'Aulike illness' is an OCR artifact for 'flu-like illness'; 'As mentioned above' under prostate cancer refers to text that is not in the source.
annotator_notes: The single hematuria episode is marked 'resolved' (the patient says his urine is back to normal now); the current absence of blood in the urine is a separate absent fact (f004).
p003, p013 and p018 support one absent fact about earlier episodes (f005) to avoid paraphrase duplicates.
Mother 'alive and healthy' is coded as an absent family-history item (no significant conditions).
The SP's CVA instruction is kept both in acting_notes and as an sp_notes exam record (x011).
